## Findings
- claim-1: The reported computational range is \(r\le4,\ n-r\le5\); thus \((r,q,i,j)=(3,6,2,2)\) lies outside it. [source-6@L46-L54|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and each proposed family has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-6@L18-L39|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: Here \(a=1,b=2,N=3\). The truncated presentation has \(65\) Schur columns, \(270\) Pieri rows, and \(1370\) direct-LR rows. The families are \(F_1=(22,32,33)\) and \(F_2=(22,221,222)\). For each \(F_\ell\), a \(62\times62\) complementary-column Pieri minor has determinant \(1\), and every direct-LR row lies in the selected Pieri lattice; direct Pieri/LR single-row mismatches were \(0\). [artifact 0b91fcbde84aa9c5a7c35b2827ba19d3c880d0cf53deaea5fad487906d234105]
- claim-4: Exact selected unit-pivot relations (each displayed expression is \(0\)); the lists are common to \(F_1,F_2\) except at degree \(6\): \[ \begin{array}{c|l} 5&(22;1):221+32\\ 6&(22;2):222+321+42;\ (221;1):42\\ 7&(22;3):322+421+52;\ (221;2):52;\ (32;2):331+43;\ (222;1):421;\ (321;1):43\\ 8&(22;4):422+521+62;\ (221;3):62;\ (32;3):332+431+53;\ (222;2):521;\ (321;2):53;\ (42;2):431+44;\ (322;1):44\\ 9&(22;5):522+621;\ (32;4):432+531+63;\ (222;3):621;\ (321;3):63;\ (33;3):333;\ (42;3):441+54;\ (322;2):531;\ (421;2):54\\ 10&(22;6):622;\ (32;5):532+631;\ (33;4):433;\ (42;4):442+541+64;\ (322;3):631;\ (421;3):64;\ (52;3):541+55;\ (422;2):55\\ 11&(32;6):632;\ (33;5):533;\ (42;5):542+641;\ (43;4):443;\ (52;4):551+65;\ (422;3):641;\ (521;3):65\\ 12&(33;6):633;\ (42;6):642;\ (43;5):543;\ (52;5):552+651;\ (44;4):444;\ (62;4):651+66;\ (522;3):66\\ 13&(43;6):643;\ (52;6):652;\ (44;5):544;\ (53;5):553;\ (62;5):661\\ 14&(44;6):644;\ (53;6):653;\ (62;6):662;\ (54;5):554\\ 15&(54;6):654;\ (63;6):663;\ (55;5):555\\ 16&(55;6):655;\ (64;6):664\\ 17&(65;6):665\\ 18&(66;6):666 \end{array} \] At degree \(6\), the third relation is \((32;1):321+33=0\) for \(F_1\), and \((32;1):-222+33=0\) for \(F_2\). [artifact 0b91fcbde84aa9c5a7c35b2827ba19d3c880d0cf53deaea5fad487906d234105]
- claim-5: Conditional on the computed row-containment assertions, the LR relation lattice equals the selected Pieri lattice in either presentation. The unimodular complementary minor makes the quotient free on the respective three free columns, so its Smith form is \(\operatorname{diag}(1^{62},0^3)\) and \(J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^3\), with basis \(F_1\) or \(F_2\).
- claim-6: The artifact records a “direct-LR” computation but does not document source code or individual LR-to-Pieri integral combinations; implementation independence and the requested independent review remain unaudited.
## Strategy
Use the supplied \(65\)-column truncated Schur presentation for \((r,q,i,j)=(3,6,2,2)\), with Pieri rows and direct-LR rows treated as separate relation sets. Audit the recorded unit-pivot transcript as successive transformed Pieri relations, yielding a complementary unimodular minor only up to sign. Compare its lattice with the direct-LR lattice by exact integral containment.

## Gaps
The preserved computation is not a genuinely independent LR/Smith implementation: enumeration and reduction share infrastructure. No coefficient vectors reducing all \(1370\) LR rows into the selected Pieri lattice are retained, and no separately computed Smith form is available. The minor sign is not certified by fixed ordered rows and columns; only determinant \(\pm1\) follows from unit pivots. The quotient interpretation also remains conditional on the box-model and Schur-span description of \(J_v\).

## Next
Implement a separate exact direct-LR matrix and integer Smith/Hermite reduction, using distinct partition/LR code. Fix row and column orders, compute the minor determinant sign, and retain integral reduction vectors for every LR row. Only then conclude whether both three-element families give integral bases of \(J_v/A_+J_v\).
